_meta.description: The pinned state of SAP's Security Baseline Template archive, so CI can tell when SAP moved.
_meta.what_this_is_not: Not the policy repository. tools/build_sap_notes_catalogue.py derives data/sap_baseline_requirements.json from SAP-samples/frun-csa-policies-best-practices, and the sap-content CI job already fails when that derivation drifts. This is the Baseline Template DOCUMENT archive, a different artefact on a different cadence.
_meta.the_gap_worth_knowing: The policy set this product derives from is v2.4. The archive currently ships V2.6. SAP's baseline document is two versions ahead of the policy content we mirror, and that is a fact about SAP's release cadence rather than a defect here — but it is the reason this record exists, because nothing else in the repository would have shown it.
_meta.why_the_change_markers_matter: Each version carries a *_change_marker.pdf. They are what makes 'the REQUIREMENT changed' distinguishable from 'the SYSTEM changed' across two scans of one estate. This check does not read them; it detects that a new one exists, which is the trigger for a person to.
_meta.no_login_wall: The URL returns HTTP 200 to an unauthenticated request. Most SAP content of this value sits behind SAP for Me; this does not, which is the only reason the check can run in CI rather than on somebody's laptop with an S-user.
_meta.how_it_is_checked: HEAD for size and timestamp, then a Range request for the last 300 KB — the archive's own central directory lists all entries, so every change worth detecting is visible at 0.3% of a 99 MB transfer.
_meta.source: docs/RISE_SECURITY_MODEL.md section 3.4 first recorded this archive; the figures here were re-measured rather than copied.
